tens_order.source: Store norske leksikon, "den nye tellemåten": "gjorde Stortinget enstemmig vedtak 22. november 1950 om å innføre den nye tellemåten"; "Den nye tellemåten ble innført fra 1. juli 1951."; "Uttalen av 23 ble for eksempel endret fra tre og tjue / tre og tyve til tjuetre." Store norske leksikon, "den gamle tellemåten": "I den gamle tellemåten settes enerleddet først, deretter og, og så tierleddet:" "21: én og tjue / én og tyve"; "Den gamle tellemåten brukes fortsatt i dagligtale, særlig blant eldre og i konservative talemålsformer." So both orders are read, and the old order is written as separate words.

ten_joins_unit_ordinal.source: The ordinal 13th is one word, "trettende", so "ten" and a unit ordinal are two numbers: CLDR RBNF nb (unicode-rbnf 2.4.1 data, no.xml), %spellout-ordinal-masculine: 1 → "første", 3 → "tredje", 4 → "fjerde", 5 → "femte", 6 → "sjette", 7 → "sjuende", 8 → "åttende", 9 → "niende", 10 → "tiende", 11 → "ellevte", 12 → "tolvte", 13 → "trettende", 19 → "nittende", 21 → "tjueførste", 30 → "trettiende", 90 → "nittiende"; Bokmålsordboka, "tjuende" (article 61230): "ordenstall til 20", where CLDR writes "tjueende"; "syvende" and "tyvende" follow "syv" and "tyve"

ordinal_joiner_by_place.source: An ordinal takes the joiner that the cardinal word in its place takes. Between a ten and a unit (never): The new order puts the unit after the ten with no joiner: CLDR RBNF nb (unicode-rbnf 2.4.1 data, no.xml), %spellout-cardinal-reale: "20: tjue[→→]"; CLDR RBNF nb (unicode-rbnf 2.4.1 data, no.xml), %spellout-numbering: 21 → "tjueén" After a hundred (optional): CLDR RBNF nb (unicode-rbnf 2.4.1 data, no.xml), %spellout-cardinal-reale: "100: hundre[ og →→]"

comma_between_classes.source: CLDR RBNF nb (unicode-rbnf 2.4.1 data, no.xml), %spellout-cardinal-reale: "1000: tusen[ →%%and-small→]" writes no comma between two classes. No source opened shows a comma between two classes of one number, so a comma ends a number.

joiner_before_last_group.source: CLDR RBNF nb (unicode-rbnf 2.4.1 data, no.xml), %spellout-cardinal-reale: "1000: tusen[ →%%and-small→]"; %and-small: "0: og =%%spellout-cardinal-reale=", "100: =%%spellout-cardinal-reale=": "og" goes before a last group below 100 and not before a round hundred ("tusen to hundre"), so the joiner before the last group is not required.

one_before_ordinal_scale_is_fraction.source: A fraction is the ordinal and "-del" ("hundredel"), so a count of one before an ordinal scale word makes an ordinal: CLDR RBNF nb (unicode-rbnf 2.4.1 data, no.xml), %spellout-ordinal-masculine: 100 → "énhundrede", 1000 → "éntusende"

period_ordinals.source: An ordinal in digits takes a period, as "17. mai" (Språkrådet, "Tal"; rule quoted from memory, the page refused automated reading). A period also ends a sentence, so only a lower-case word after it, as month names are (CLDR month names for Norwegian Bokmål (Babel 2.18.0): "januar", "februar", "mars", "april", "mai", "juni", "juli", "august", "september", "oktober", "november", "desember"; Bokmålsordboka, "mai" (article 36582): headword "mai", "årets femte måned"), or "den" before the digits makes it an ordinal mark: "i 1905. Dette" is the cardinal 1905.
